recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is for FHIR-18650. Handle any further Implicit Code Systems wording or status treatment through newer R6 tickets and Vocabulary work-group decisions, not by reopening the STU3 status-marker ballot comment.
issue_request: FHIR-18650 was a Published STU3 Vocabulary/CodeSystem issue with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. It asked that the section about relationships between rich terminologies and structured content be marked Trial Use because the section had a yellowish status background; the accepted modification was not to mark it Trial Use, because the section was a lower-status informative marker, but to make the status-marker text clearer.
initial_application: The Jira comment identifies git 4907f9bcb0b710cb2837a93a20c4b23210a37249 as the application. That commit changed the CodeSystem notes box from old informative-content wording to an explicit linked draft-content/draft-flag status label and added distinct CSS marker classes for informative, draft, trial-use, and deprecated states.
additional_context: CodeSystem remains an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini and belongs to the Vocabulary work group. Later same-section decisions changed the current target: FHIR-39265 was Published/Persuasive and commented out the draft implicit-code-systems section because the draft/under-review box was confusing; FHIR-40432 was Applied/Persuasive and restored a rewritten Implicit Code Systems section. The current source has the restored heading and explanatory content without the old colored informative/draft/Trial Use status box, while the shared CSS still distinguishes formal status markers.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build no longer contains the STU3 wording or colored section marker that FHIR-18650 addressed, and adding a Trial Use or informative box now would overrule later Vocabulary decisions rather than complete the seed issue.
